answers.reason: Covers the ¶11 duty that all drugs be manufactured per CGMP regulations; mandatory 'must' preserved, nothing added.
States the ¶11 'must' that prescription-drug records be readily available for review; scope limited to prescription drugs as in the text.
Matches the ¶11 statement that all prescription and OTC manufacturers must comply with CGMPR including record requirements.
¶14 requires a quality control department with the CFR-described responsibility and authority; 'unit' vs 'department' and 'CGMP regulations' vs 'referenced CFR' do not change the obligation.
Restates the ¶14 'must maintain its independence from the production department' for the QC unit at mandatory strength.
¶14 says QC responsibilities must be in writing; the statement asks exactly that at mandatory strength.
¶16 'should be documented' for training received by an employee; recommended strength and scope match.
¶17 'Quality control must do product annual review on each drug manufactured' is reproduced fully and mandatory.
¶17 requires written annual review procedures; statement matches at mandatory strength.
¶17 'should provide a summary' of all lots failing in-process or finished testing and other critical factors; all elements kept, recommended.
¶17 instructs 'Investigate any failures' in the annual-review context; the statement uses the same words and recommended strength.
¶18 'Quality control must validate the manufacturing process for each drug manufactured' reproduced with QC as actor, mandatory.
¶20 lighting, ventilation, screening and barriers for all operations incl. dust, temperature, humidity, bacteriological controls; all listed elements kept.
¶20 'must be adequate blueprints' of high purity water, HEPA and compressed air systems; all three systems kept, mandatory.
¶20 site must have adequate locker, toilet and hand washing facilities; statement matches.
List item ¶22 combined with ¶21 lead-in (adequate space for equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups); receiving, sampling, storage of raw materials all present.
List item ¶23 'manufacturing or processing' with the ¶21 lead-in purpose of preventing mix-ups; mandatory from 'must provide'.
List item ¶24 'packaging and labeling' with full ¶21 lead-in (space for equipment and materials to prevent mix-ups).
List item ¶25 storage of containers, packaging materials, labeling and finished products, with the ¶21 lead-in condition intact.
List item ¶26 production and control laboratories with the ¶21 adequate-space-to-prevent-mix-ups lead-in; mandatory.
¶28 'New equipment must be properly installed, and operate as designed'; 'new' qualifier kept, mandatory.
¶28 investigator instruction to determine if an equipment change requires FDA pre-approval and/or revalidation; condition of an equipment change is in the statement, recommended.
¶28 equipment must be cleaned before use according to written procedures; 'before use' and 'written procedures' kept.
¶28 'The cleaning must be documented and validated' - both documentation and validation retained.
¶29 'should not adversely effect the identity, strength, quality, or purity'; all four attributes and recommended strength kept.
¶29 'material used to manufacture the equipment must not react with the drug'; mandatory matches.
¶29 'lubricants or coolants must not contaminate the drug'; mandatory matches.
¶30 equipment 'should be constructed and located to ease cleaning, adjustments, and maintenance'; recommended, all three purposes kept.
¶30 equipment 'should prevent contamination from other or previous manufacturing operations'; recommended strength, both sources of contamination kept.
¶30 equipment must be identified as to cleaning status and content; both attributes kept, mandatory.
¶30 investigator determination of suitable capacity and accuracy for measuring, weighing or mixing; expects the practice, recommended.
¶30 conditional 'If the equipment requires calibration' is in the statement; written procedure and documented calibration both required, mandatory.
¶32 'They must have written procedures' for the listed component/container/closure operations; statement spells out all operations (received ... approved or rejected).
¶32 conditional computer control of component handling and storage stated; 'program must be validated' mandatory.
¶33 receiving records must provide traceability to component manufacturer and supplier; both kept, mandatory.
¶33 receiving records 'should contain' component name, manufacturer, supplier if different, and carrier; all four elements and the 'if different' qualifier kept.
¶33 records should also include receiving date, manufacturer's lot number, quantity received and firm-assigned control number; all four kept, recommended.
¶36 investigator determination that colors are approved for intended use and required statements are declared on the label; both parts kept, recommended.
¶37 components must be handled per drug CGMPs, explicitly including R&D lab components; that scope extension is kept.
¶37 'Determine how components are identified after receipt and quarantined until released' expects identification and quarantine until release; recommended.
¶37 components must be identified so status (quarantine, approved, rejected) is known; all three statuses kept, mandatory.
¶38 asks whether component sampling/testing procedures and release process are adequate and followed; statement asks for adequacy and adherence, recommended.
¶39 determination of validity and accuracy of the inventory system for components, containers, closures and labeling; all four material types kept.
¶39 'Significant discrepancies in these records should be investigated'; 'significant' qualifier kept, recommended.
¶40 lead-in: firm has shown containers/closures compatible, protective against deterioration or contamination, not additive or absorptive, suitable; all four criteria kept.
List item ¶41 (specifications for containers, closures, cotton filler, desiccant) tied to the ¶40 lead-in purpose; recommended from the 'Evaluate' lead-in.
List item ¶42 tests/checks with its examples, linked to the ¶40 lead-in demonstration of suitability; recommended.
List item ¶43 cleaning procedures and container storage, with the ¶40 lead-in purpose stated; recommended.
¶44 'The firm must review the labeling for accuracy' in the context of preprinted containers; statement keeps the preprinted-container scope and mandatory 'must'.
¶47 'shall' - each critical step done by a responsible individual and checked by a second; both individuals kept, mandatory.
¶47 conditional automatic mechanical or electronic control of such steps is in the statement; 'should be verified' recommended.
¶48 critical steps documented when done, not before or after the fact; recommended descriptive expectation, nothing added.
¶50 all containers and equipment used to manufacture a drug 'should be labeled at all times'; 'at all times' kept, recommended.
¶50 label should identify contents including batch number and stage of processing; all elements kept.
¶50 'Previous identification labels should be removed' restated at recommended strength.
¶50 batch should be handled and stored to prevent mixups or contamination; both hazards kept, recommended.

¶52 'shall be adequate in-process controls' for uniformity and integrity with all listed examples (tablet weight/disintegration, liquid fill, mixing, suspension homogeneity, solution clarity); mandatory.
¶53 investigator check that in-process test equipment is on site and specified tests done; both elements kept, recommended.
¶55 personnel check actual against theoretical yield of each batch; 'each batch' kept, recommended.
¶55 significant unexplained discrepancy condition is in the statement; procedure to prevent distribution of the batch and related batches kept.
¶61 tableting equipment constructed/located to facilitate maintenance and cleaning at end of each batch or suitable intervals for continuous operation; OSD only, recommended.
¶61 'determine if the cleaning procedure is followed' for tableting equipment; 'if possible' qualifies only the investigator's observation, so nothing is dropped; OSD.
¶63 mixing, granulation, drying and/or tableting segregated in enclosed areas with own air handling to prevent cross-contamination; purpose and all operations kept, OSD.
¶64 determination that powders or granulations are processed per the firm's specifications; recommended, OSD tablet context.
¶64 'The mixing process must be validated' in the tablet section; mandatory, OSD.
¶64 drying ovens should have own air handling system preventing cross-contamination; recommended, purpose kept.
¶64 inspection question on recording drying time/temperature and keeping charts incl. LOD results; all elements kept, recommended.
¶65 powders for capsules should follow the same practice as tablets; recommended, OSD.
¶67 'Parenteral drugs must be non-pyrogenic'; mandatory, limited to INJ.
¶67 any condition permitting bacterial growth should be avoided in the (parenteral) manufacturing process; recommended, INJ.
¶69 procedures to minimize contamination of sterile drugs with microorganisms and particulates; both contaminant types kept, INJ.
¶70 personnel performing production and control procedures have experience and training commensurate with duties; sterile-section scope expressed, INJ, recommended.
¶70 'It is important that personnel be trained in aseptic procedures' read as recommended; sterile scope, INJ.
¶70 employees must be properly gowned and use good aseptic techniques; both elements kept, mandatory, INJ.
¶71 non-sterile preparation areas for sterile drugs should be controlled; scope 'for sterile drugs' kept, recommended.
¶71 determination of how the firm minimizes traffic and unnecessary activity in the (sterile) preparation area; recommended, INJ.
¶71 filling rooms and other aseptic areas constructed to eliminate microbiological/particulate contamination sites, with ledges and porous surfaces as examples; recommended.
¶72 air to non-sterile preparation/formulation areas for solutions prior to sterilization filtered as necessary to control particulates; 'as necessary' kept, recommended.
¶72 air to product exposure areas for sterile drugs should be HEPA filtered under positive pressure; both HEPA and positive pressure kept.
¶73 HEPA filters certified and/or DOP tested and the frequency of testing reviewed; 'and/or' and frequency kept, recommended.
¶74 compressed air filtered at point of use to control particulates; point-of-use qualifier kept, recommended, sterile section INJ.
¶75 specifications for viable and non-viable particulates must be established; both types kept, mandatory.
¶75 viable particulate specifications must provide for both air and surface sampling of aseptic areas and equipment; nothing dropped.
¶75 determine if firm follows its procedure for reviewing out-of-limit (environmental) test results; recommended.
¶75 review of environmental test data included in the firm's release procedures; recommended, nothing added beyond 'batch' wording.
¶76 suitable inactivating agents should be added to environmental sampling media, with the penicillinase example for penicillin and cephalosporin operations; recommended.
